review_scope: Coordinator fully read all three primary transcripts and adjudicated every complete composed answer, separately from runtime context checks. Same-team captured-text development review, not external blind or live certification.

cases.question: What exactly was Kat trying to collect, and why Japanese Pockets?
cases.query: Kat Japanese Pocket basic colors boxes aesthetics
cases.answer: Kat was prioritizing basic-color Game Boy Pockets complete in Japanese boxes, because she liked their appearance and packaging. She already had pink and Christmas clear-purple units. She believed there were nine basic colors, and mentioned off-white original-style and perhaps extreme green as extra wants—not a commitment to every limited edition or a full game library.
cases.reason: P3–5/P34–35 support owned colors and scoped goal; nine is qualified historical belief.

cases.question: How did Johnny get the gold Game Boy Light?
cases.query: Johnny gold Light forgot Zelda magazine
cases.answer: The episode cannot establish where or why he originally got it. Johnny rediscovered it behind a Zelda II Nintendo Fun Club magazine and explicitly said he did not know its origin. He later guessed he had bought it because it was gold and would fit his Zelda display. That is speculation, unlike his definite report of recently playing Dr. Mario in it.
cases.reason: P17/P19 explicitly uncertain provenance/motive distinct from definite Dr Mario play.

cases.question: Why does the episode talk about smuggling Game Boys?
cases.query: Micro prison smuggling Kat joke
cases.answer: It is a hardware-size joke that grows out of whether a Micro would fit a formal occasion. The Micro is the preferred hypothetical smuggling system, with the Light and SP floated as alternatives. Kat says she has never been to prison and is not planning to go; Johnny invites listeners to ask her which Game Boy she would smuggle. This is a callback, not either host's criminal biography.
cases.reason: P23–27 full source clearly hypothetical joke and Kat denial; callback not biography.

cases.question: Who had actually played Child of Light, and how much?
cases.query: Child of Light Kat Johnny Xbox Gold
cases.answer: Johnny had played about 30 minutes on Xbox One, enjoyed it, and thought he had obtained it through Gold. Kat had it ready on Xbox One and planned to start after recording, but said she had not played it yet. Neither reports finishing the game.
cases.reason: P43–44 distinguish Kat future intent from Johnny limited play and uncertain Gold source.

cases.answer: Johnny picked up Wario Land 3 and Shantae for the Nintendo Power 285 project and says both are complete in box; he especially praises Shantae's mint condition. He describes Shantae as expensive rather than rare-rare, an episode opinion, not a verified market assessment. A further Game Boy item has an accepted offer and is still coming, but is unnamed. His Shantae sequel names and platform history are explicitly uncertain, so the episode cannot confidently identify those sequels.
forbidden: Shantae sequel names normalized as fact
cases.reason: P40–43 named CIB pickups versus separate unnamed incoming item, no sequel cleanup.

cases.query: Deja Vu Shadowgate Princess Tomato Kat Johnny
cases.answer: Johnny likes Deja Vu and Shadowgate, describing Deja Vu as a spiritual successor rather than a sequel and correcting 'text adventure' to point-and-click. cases.question: What Game & Watch games were picked up, and were they tested?
cases.query: Chef Manhole Ball box untested
cases.answer: Kat got Chef and Manhole locally. They were her only two Game & Watch games, and she had not tried either, so she did not know whether they worked or were fun. One had a worn box; she thought Chef but was unsure. Johnny's only example was the Club Nintendo Ball remake, not an original unit.
cases.reason: P39–40 untested acquisitions and uncertain box assignment; Ball remake separate.

cases.question: Why virtual pinball, and did Johnny buy a cabinet?
cases.query: Pinball Arcade Metroid pinball cabinet remodel
cases.answer: Johnny was playing The Pinball Arcade on PS4 and liked virtual pinball's consequence-free retries and table selection. He reports buying packs over time with roughly 40 tables available, not 40 physical machines. He also likes DS Metroid pinball's two-screen verticality and recalls loving NES Pinball. He owns a physical pinball machine needing a flipper repair, but only wants a small virtual cabinet. He will not divert normal remodeling finances; a separate fund would depend on selling spare items, so no cabinet purchase or completed funding sale is established.
cases.reason: P44–46 virtual-game play/pack ownership, physical repair, desired cabinet and conditional funding all distinct.

cases.question: Was Johnny's first portable the NES-style SP or his wife's GBA?
cases.query: first portable Game Boy Advance SP girlfriend
cases.answer: Those describe different milestones. Johnny says he had no childhood portable and first encountered handheld ownership through his then-girlfriend's GBA in the mid-2000s. The NES-styled Game Boy SP was the first portable he personally bought that was not his wife's. He later bought further DS/3DS iterations, but missed the Animal Crossing-themed one he wanted.
cases.reason: P2/P30–31 separate exposure/household access from own purchase, no AnimalCrossing ownership.

cases.question: What should I watch for when collecting SMB3 variants?
cases.query: Mario 3 left Bros box manual cart incorrect
cases.answer: They discuss the left-positioned Bros version and say the box, manual and cartridge should match. Relative rarity does not make it genuinely scarce in their account because production was large. The incorrect-manual stories illustrate why matching pieces matters; prices and rarity estimates are historical speaker claims, not current verified guidance.
cases.reason: P7–9 supports left-positioned Bros matching across box/manual/cart, relative-versus-absolute rarity and mismatched-manual anecdotes without current price claims.

cases.question: How do Kat, Tyler and Johnny differ on Mario favorites?
cases.query: favorite Paper Mario Mario Kart Tyler 64 Galaxy Sunshine
cases.answer: Kat names N64 Paper Mario and Mario Kart, with nostalgia and continued enjoyment. Tyler chooses Super Mario 64 at the close. Johnny loves the original Super Mario Bros. and names the first Galaxy for 3D Mario, while Odyssey might overtake it after more play. Sunshine is divisive: Johnny dislikes it, Tyler defends it, and Kat says she stopped after about five minutes.
cases.reason: P11–13 and38 preserve Kat's Paper Mario/Kart nostalgia, Tyler's64 preference, Johnny's SMB/Galaxy with provisional Odyssey contender, and real Sunshine disagreement.

cases.question: Did everyone own the Odyssey coin?
cases.query: coin Odyssey Galaxy wrapper cardboard sleeve four send
cases.answer: No. The discussion switches from an assumed Odyssey coin to the Galaxy coin, and the speakers correct what they mean. Opened-wrapper, kept-box and unopened-copy statements cannot safely be merged into one person's Galaxy inventory. After clarification, one speaker says they have roughly four Galaxy coins and offers to send some; that is not evidence of delivery.
cases.reason: P27 changes the referent from Odyssey to Galaxy mid-dialogue; unknown actors and an offered rather than delivered coin are appropriately retained.

cases.question: What did the hosts get this week, and what remains unplayed?
cases.query: purchased week Tyler Virtual Fighter Remix Tailgate Party Cat Call of Duty Shockman
cases.answer: Tyler says Virtua Fighter Remix arrived in the Saturn long box and explicitly has not played it. He also received Tailgate Party, praising its power-pad cornhole concept. Kat bought an unspecified Call of Duty on Xbox but has not played it because John is using it. Johnny bought a Shockman cartridge through Archon Turtle, completing the box he already owned.
cases.reason: P39/40/44 supports Tyler receipt/unplayed Remix and Tailgate Party, Kat unspecified Xbox Call of Duty unplayed, and Johnny cart-only Shockman completion.

cases.answer: Not safely. The closing summary says they are all kind of playing Odyssey, but the later conversation explicitly singles out Kat as lacking time and says she has not played it. Her Call of Duty purchase is also unplayed at this point. Those specific qualifications take priority over a loose group statement.
cases.reason: Specific Kat nonplay inP40/43 qualifies loose all-playing summaryP38; no invented completion or dated play transition.

cases.question: Does Johnny recommend Rabbids from experience, and does Kat love it?
cases.query: Rabbids special edition did not buy Cat loves Life Strange prequel
cases.answer: Johnny explicitly passed on the large Kingdom Battle special edition despite liking Switch editions, and the hosts do not claim to have played it. Reports that it is good are hearsay, not his own review. The claim that Kat loves Rabbids is a tease she denies; it leads into their Life Is Strange disagreement and Johnny's intention to play the prequel, not proof he already did.
cases.reason: P30–32 supports declined large edition, no firsthand review, Kat denying tease, and intended rather than completed prequel play.
